messages:
liang: Heads-up — after the CUDA driver rollout this morning we're seeing a consistent small-batch (B=1/2) p99 latency spike on H100 and A100 nodes. Perf traces attached to the ticket, but quick summary: +12% p99, median ~unchanged.

maya: ugh. any obvious diff in kernel selection or batching?

liang: digging in. Autotuner is now choosing the "long-seq" kernel path for short sequences in several hot models. Looks like the new driver slightly changed warp scheduler timings and the heuristics that pick kernels now prefer larger-block GEMM for many shapes. That interacts badly with our continuous-batching path and forces an extra KV memcpy for cached prefix requests.

connor: can you paste the perf snippet? nvprof / nsight findings?

liang: sure — nvprof shows 1) chosen kernel = gemm_fused_longseq_v2 instead of small_batch_opt, 2) ~200us extra memcpy for KV scatter on first token, 3) higher tail due to extra copy + non-optimal block size on seq<=64. Snippet:```Kernel: gemm_fused_longseq_v2 time: 0.86ms memcpy(kv): 0.22ms
Kernel: small_batch_opt time: 0.78ms memcpy(kv): 0.01ms```

devon: so two components — kernel pick and KV memcpy path. Can we short-circuit the memcpy in runtime for cached requests?

liang: we can, but that change needs careful testing. Two immediate mitigations: 1) force the legacy small-batch kernel for affected model families via runtime flag; 2) disable autotune for short-seq profiles until we validate. Both are low-risk and reversible.

maya: prefer quick mitigation: disable autotune for seq<=64 and roll a canary. What's the CLI/patch?

liang: temporary config we can push to dedicated fleets:```{
  "autotune": {"enabled": true, "seq_threshold": 64, "override_for_short_seq": false}
}
# or runtime flag: --force-kernel=small_batch_opt --kernel-scope=model:openllama-3b
```

connor: ops-bot can we run a canary with ~5% traffic to rollback-driver AND a canary with autotune-off to compare? want to see which is cheaper.

ops-bot: deploy job queued: canary-autotune-off -> 5% traffic on prod-gpu-pool-2 (H100), expected rollout 10m; canary-driver-rollback -> 5% traffic on same pool via node selector to driver-12 nodes, expected rollout 20m. Will post links when live. :gear:

maya: monitoring watchers: set alerts for p99 > baseline+5% and token/s drop > 3%. Dashboards to watch: /console/dashboards/latency/small-batch, /console/dashboards/kv-cache-ops.

devon: longer term fixes: 1) make kernel-selection autotuner include driver-sensitive features (driver version, microarch flags) in the feature vector; 2) detect memcpy regressions and prefer kernel with smaller memory traffic for cached paths; 3) add a runtime policy to avoid long-seq kernel path when batch_size<=2 and seq<=64.

liang: agreed. I'll open a spec for the autotuner feature-vector change and a small runtime patch to add the short-seq safety guard. For now I'll push the autotune-off canary and the kernel-force patch for the most affected model families.

connor: thanks. please include perf traces and exact rollout IDs in the ticket. Also add a quick playbook entry for on-call: how to flip the kernel flag and how to revert.

liang: will do — ticket RF#6428. TL;DR: immediate -> canary disable-autotune, force small_batch_opt for hot models. Medium -> runtime short-seq guard. Long -> autotuner model+driver feature expansion.

maya: :thumbsup: keep the thread updated when canaries finish.

ops-bot: canary-autotune-off live: https://console/redwood/canaries/1841234567-autotune-off, status: running, started_at: 1841234700

liang: canary results (prelim): autotune-off canary reduced p99 by ~9% vs baseline on H100; driver-rollback canary still pending. Will post final numbers in ticket.

maya: great, schedule the rollback of the driver rollout to the <=12 nodes only if rollback canary beats autotune-off? we should prefer software mitigation first.

liang: agreed. Locking plan: software-first, driver rollback only if software path fails or causes regressions elsewhere.

devon: add a note to release notes and internal postmortem when resolved.

liang: done. closing loop later with final perf artifacts.
